cases.name: corpus-allow-quoted-heredoc-commit
cases.command:
git commit -F - <<'MSG'
docs: prefer the narrow git command over the overloaded one

`checkout` and `reset` each cover several unrelated jobs under one name.
During R4.2's Task 12 a subagent ran `git checkout --` against a test file
without checking `git status` first and discarded uncommitted work. It
restored the file from a backup, but the loss was unverifiable in principle:
`git checkout -- <file>` never moves HEAD, so it writes no reflog entry and
there is nothing left to diff a restore against.

The rule is picked by intent rather than by command name, because `revert`
and `reset --hard` are not substitutes for each other — `revert` stacks a new
commit and leaves shared history valid, `reset --hard` cuts history off. Both
keep their place; only the default changes.

`reset --hard` stays available for the case that genuinely needs it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
git log --oneline -1
cases.why: A real commit message in a quoted heredoc that quotes git checkout -- inside backticks.

cases.name: settled-allow-operandless-checkout-in-a-heredoc
cases.command:
git commit -F - <<EOF
never `git checkout` here
EOF
cases.why: The body is read, and what it holds is a checkout with no operand, which this rule allows. Both settlements hold at once, and this is where they meet.
